findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Compromise of this user's credentials would allow reading or destroying all S3 data, launching or terminating any EC2 instance, and modifying Lambda functions — including privilege-escalation paths such as attaching existing instance profiles or altering Lambda execution code.

A permanent IAM access key is provisioned for a user holding wildcard permissions, and no pgp_key is supplied, so the secret access key is written to Terraform state in cleartext. Static, non-rotating keys stored in state are a well-known credential-leak vector compared with temporary role-based credentials.

The "secret" output exports access key material from the module. Since no pgp_key was set, encrypted_secret is unpopulated and the plaintext secret resides in state; exporting it propagates the credential of a highly privileged user to consuming modules, CI logs, and anyone with state access. The output is also not marked sensitive.

findings.issue_category: privileged IAM user with inline policy
findings.description: A standalone IAM user carries an inline wildcard policy instead of permissions granted through a group or an assumable role with temporary credentials, and has no MFA requirement or permission boundary. This creates a persistent, highly privileged identity that is hard to review, constrain, or revoke centrally.
